package_info.why_malicious: The report does not describe a specific malicious package, but rather outlines general cybercriminal tactics and tools targeting e-commerce platforms and shoppers during the holiday season. It highlights the use of AI-powered phishing, website cloning, sniffers, and RCE exploits, but does not provide code or package-level details.

behavioral_signatures: AI-generated phishing emails mimicking retailers or banks
Registration and use of holiday-themed domains similar to trusted brands
Deployment of sniffers to intercept payment data during online transactions
Exploitation of RCE vulnerabilities in e-commerce platforms
Use of phishing kits and website cloning tools
file_indicators: Phishing kit templates resembling retailer login pages
Sniffer scripts embedded in e-commerce checkout pages
Malicious plugins or scripts in outdated e-commerce platform directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains registered with holiday or retailer-themed names
Traffic to known phishing or exfiltration endpoints
Unusual POST requests from checkout or login pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the registration and use of domains closely resembling legitimate retailer brands, especially with holiday themes. Detect AI-generated or template-based phishing emails targeting customers. Scan e-commerce platforms for unauthorized scripts or plugins, especially those that intercept form data or initiate outbound network connections. Watch for exploitation attempts against known RCE vulnerabilities in e-commerce software. Use behavioral analytics to flag unusual login attempts, brute-force activity, or data exfiltration from checkout pages.
